title: Stories of Ancient Stones: A Living Tradition of Indigenous People (Mundas) in Jharkhand, India

identity_reconciliation.disposition: Upgrade the existing permanent MMSC identity; do not count the publisher article page, issue PDF, DOI landing page, or author profile as separate intellectual works.

exact_locators.bounded_proposition: The issue PDF identifies the article, authors, recommended citation, DOI 10.30884/seh/2025.02.01, article span pp. 3-26, and publisher copyright notice.

exact_locators.locator: article printed p. 12 / issue PDF index 11, Research Design and Participant Selection
exact_locators.bounded_proposition: The authors describe a qualitative ethnographic/participatory design focused on Munda villages in Ranchi and report a study sample of 15 Munda participants aged 18-70 selected using initial contacts and snowball recruitment.

exact_locators.locator: article printed pp. 13-14 / issue PDF indexes 12-13, Data Collection and Ethical Considerations
exact_locators.bounded_proposition: The authors report participant observation, interviews, oral narratives and participatory methods; they also report informing participants about the research and withdrawal rights, obtaining verbal consent, using pseudonyms/confidentiality, restricting sensitive information to express permission, and consulting community leaders and elders.

rights_access_governance.journal_policy_summary: The journal states a BOAI-aligned open-access policy permitting users to read, download, copy, distribute, print, search, link and otherwise lawfully use full texts without access barriers.
rights_access_governance.current_ingestion_boundary: Promote bibliographic, study-scope, methods and reported-ethics facts only. Do not ingest participant names/pseudonyms, ages, quotations, interview content, oral narratives, ritual details, culturally sensitive site information, images, transcripts or field notes without separate item-level rights, consent and cultural-access review.

participant_privacy_and_cultural_sensiti.reason: The article is participant-derived ethnography and includes potentially sensitive cultural material. Article-level access does not replace MLHKP dignity, consent, purpose-limitation and cultural-access controls.
